Compare a change on matched cases

Source: R/compare-trajectories.R
compare_trajectories.Rd

compare_trajectories() reads a pairing from pair_trajectories() and reports what changed between the baseline and the candidate for each matched case. It reads the saved evaluations, scanner assessments, and resource measures of the two investigations. It never runs a solver, a scorer, a scanner, or a model.

Usage

compare_trajectories(pairing, conf_level = 0.95)

Arguments

pairing

A scans_pairing value from pair_trajectories(). The investigations it holds must be valid and carry the snapshot and revision identifiers the pairing recorded.

conf_level

Confidence level for intervals, between 0 and 1.

Value

A scans_comparison value: a list with the pairing, the design (type and reason), per-case tibbles outcomes, patterns, and resources, a cases tibble with one row per pair counting its changes in each family, and summaries (a list of outcomes, patterns, and resources tibbles). Printing leads with what could not be compared.

Details

Changes come in three families that are never combined into one score:

  • outcomes: one row per case and scorer. A change is reported only for a compatible scorer pair whose values are on the declared scale.

  • patterns: one row per case and scan: "appeared", "resolved", "persisted", "absent", or "not_comparable" when either side was not assessed, did not run the scan, or ran it under a different version or settings. A pattern found on one side whose scan does not apply to the other side's capture is "no_longer_applicable" (found on the baseline) or "newly_applicable" (found on the candidate): the pattern could not occur in the other capture, which is not a fix or a regression. These are counted on their own and never feed the share resolved or its test. A scan that does not apply, with no finding on the other side, is absent.

  • resources: one row per case and measure. A delta is reported only when both sides have a recorded value with complete coverage under the same unit, aggregation, source, measurement contract, and cache inclusion. Otherwise the delta is NA and reason says why. A higher resource value is not labelled better or worse.

Every row carries both trajectory identities. Pattern rows also carry the finding and event identities on each side.

Summaries

The estimand is a change among paired cases from the same dataset version. summaries counts cases by direction for each scorer, scan, and measure. A scorer with no comparable outcome keeps a row with n zero and its n_not_comparable count. When each case has one pair and at least six cases changed, it adds the share of changed cases that moved in the named direction, an exact (Clopper-Pearson) interval for that share, and an exact two-sided sign test of an even split. For a binary scorer this is the exact McNemar test. With fewer changed cases, or with repeated epochs, summaries are counts only and note says why. P-values are per row and unadjusted. Two descriptive numbers have no interval and are reported whatever the number of changed cases: paired_difference, the difference in the proportion at the better level for a binary scorer without repeated epochs, and median_delta for numeric outcomes and resources.

When no case pairs, for example under different dataset versions, the design is "unpaired": summaries describes each side separately, every table is labelled "unpaired", and no paired estimate, interval, or test is produced.

A recorded difference between two runs does not establish that the change caused it. See vignette("matched-comparison") for what a result supports.

Examples

bundle <- function(score) {
  TrajectoryBundle(
    data.frame(
      trajectory_id = "run-1",
      sample_id = "case-1",
      source_type = "manual",
      status = "completed"
    ),
    data.frame(),
    data.frame(),
    evaluations = tibble::tibble(
      trajectory_id = "run-1",
      evaluation_id = "run-1/evaluation",
      scorer = "judge",
      value = list(score)
    )
  )
}
if (rlang::is_installed(c("digest", "jsonlite"))) {
  pairing <- pair_trajectories(
    investigation_snapshot(bundle(0), application = "Baseline"),
    investigation_snapshot(bundle(1), application = "Candidate"),
    by = "sample_id",
    dataset_version = "2026-11",
    scorers = list(comparison_scorer("judge", "1", "numeric"))
  )
  comparison <- compare_trajectories(pairing)
  comparison$outcomes[c("sample_id", "baseline_value", "candidate_value", "change")]
  comparison
}
